title: What If a Day on Earth Lasted 47 of Today's Days?

scenes.text: What if one day on Earth lasted 47 of today's days? The Moon is already pushing us there.
The Moon drifts away about 3.8 centimeters every year, and it slows Earth's spin as it goes.
Tidal friction stretches our day by about one second every 40,000 years.
Eventually Earth's spin and the Moon's orbit would match, both taking about 47 days.
The Moon would then stay fixed in the sky over one side of Earth, around 560,000 kilometers away.
But the Sun would swell into a red giant first, and could engulf both worlds before it ever happens.
